issues.legal_issue: A charitable arrangement creates a trust only when the donor intends to extinguish private title through complete dedication; otherwise, the property remains private and is subject to a charge for the charity.
material_facts: A prior registered deed had dedicated property to public charities and required the whole income to be used only for those purposes.
A later compromise decree partitioned the property between the donor and his son and allotted some property to the donor.
The decree described the donor as sole trustee during his lifetime, allowed him to enjoy the property, and required income to be used for the charities according to their needs.

The decree directed that the property pass after the donor’s death to his grandson subject to the charities, and allowed the grandson to enjoy the property and conduct the charities without a restriction on his dealing with it.
The parties agreed that the property in the appellants’ hands remained burdened by the obligation to perform the charities.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree did not create a public charitable trust in the allotted property; the property remained private and was subject to a charge for the charities. The suit for a scheme was therefore dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, whether a charitable dedication is complete depends on the donor’s intention, gathered from a fair construction of the document as a whole. Complete dedication creates a trust; partial dedication leaves the property’s private character intact and creates a charge. Use of the words “trust” or “trustee” is not conclusive; the central test is whether private title was intended to be extinguished. The Court relied on Maharani Hemanta Kumari Debi v. Gauri Shankar Tewari, Jadu Nath Singh v. Thakur Sita Ramji, Pande Har Narayan v. Surja Kunwari, Sonatun Bysack v. Sreemutti Juggutsoondyee Dossee, Gopal Lal Sett v. Purna Chandra Basak, and Chairman of the Howrah Municipality v. Khetra Krishna Mitra. The suit was brought under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

predicates.charity_scheme_suit: The proceeding seeks a scheme for administering property alleged to be held in trust for public charity.
predicates.charitable_obligation_attaches_to_proper: The governing arrangement requires the property or its income to support specified charitable purposes.
predicates.private_enjoyment_or_succession_is_retai: The arrangement allows a private individual to enjoy the property or provides for it to pass by private succession.
predicates.charitable_income_is_limited_to_need: The arrangement requires only such income as the charities need to be used for them, rather than dedicating all income exclusively to charity.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks a scheme for charitable property, a charitable obligation attaches to the property, and private enjoyment or succession is retained or charitable income is limited to need, the property remains private subject to a charitable charge rather than becoming trust property.

issues.legal_issue: A party that acquiesces in a finding that a compromise displaced an earlier trust and pursues a claim only on the basis that the compromise created a new trust cannot later advance an inconsistent claim that the earlier trust remained unaffected.
material_facts: The plaintiffs originally sought a scheme for the trust created by the earlier deed, but the trial court proceeded on the basis that the compromise had displaced that trust and created a new trust.
The plaintiffs did not appeal the finding that the compromise bound the earlier trust and did not seek a scheme on the basis that the earlier trust remained in force.
Before the High Court, the plaintiffs argued that the compromise itself created a trust in the properties allotted to the donor.
The findings that the compromise was not collusive or fraudulent and bound the trust were not challenged by the plaintiffs.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not raise the inconsistent contention that the compromise did not bind the earlier trust and that the earlier trust remained unaffected; the Court did not consider the merits of that contention.
issues.legal_principle: In the procedural circumstances of this case, the plaintiffs’ acquiescence in the finding that the compromise bound the earlier trust, their failure to appeal or seek a scheme on the earlier trust’s basis, and their reliance on the compromise as creating a new trust amounted to an admission that the earlier trust had been displaced. They could not later advance the inconsistent position.

rule.if: charity_scheme_appeal and trial_decision_treats_later_arrangement_as_replacing_earlier_trust and claimant_does_not_appeal_that_basis and claimant_advances_only_later_trust_basis

predicates.charity_scheme_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a suit seeking a scheme for the administration of a charitable trust.
predicates.trial_decision_treats_later_arrangement_: The trial court bases its relief on the conclusion that a later arrangement displaced an earlier trust and created a substituted trust.
predicates.claimant_does_not_appeal_that_basis: The claimant does not appeal the finding that the later arrangement binds or replaces the earlier trust, and does not seek relief on the basis that the earlier trust remains in force.
predicates.claimant_advances_only_later_trust_basis: The claimant argues that the later arrangement itself created the trust on which the requested relief rests.

issues.definition: In a charity-scheme appeal, a claimant who does not challenge the finding that a later arrangement replaced an earlier trust and relies only on the later trust cannot advance the inconsistent claim that the earlier trust survived.
